alternatives.option: Key retention on the parsed body id only (add fileIds after a successful parse)
alternatives.reason_rejected: cannot retain for the unreadable classes (markers, 0-byte, I/O error) — exactly the field's failure mode; the stem is the only identity available before parsing

alternatives.option: Treat an unparseable file as absent and let the row delete (status quo, documented)
alternatives.reason_rejected: silently loses committed history on every host that merges a conflicted file; the embedding is swept as an orphan and the repaired record re-inserts as a NEW row (seq churn, vector regenerated)

alternatives.option: Insert a parseable id≠stem body under its body id (pre-fix behavior)
alternatives.reason_rejected: creates a stray row the deletion pass will remove next cycle while the stem row is deleted now — two wrong rows from one mis-keyed file

context: 2.16.1 Task 1: ingest retention keyed on the filename stem — a record file that exists but cannot be read or identified never deletes its sqlite row; non-string id now counted+warned; id≠stem refused
rationale: Workflow wf_daceaa5d-eee lane V2 EXECUTED the deletion at HEAD d649ec4 (conflict markers, 0-byte, non-string id, id≠stem all deleted the row while the file stayed on disk; docblock :19 promised the opposite; the old test never seeded a row so deleted was trivially 0). Field relevance: their tier-A merge queue evicts conflicted records/ entries and every host that ingests the tree deletes that ULID's row — presenting as an EMPTY assemble (host-B symptom). Stem-keyed retention (`if (dbRows.has(stem)) fileIds.add(stem)`) runs before readRecord so every failure class retains. The correctness critic's id≠stem case is refused instead of inserted under the wrong key: a stray row under the body id plus deletion of the stem row was the pre-fix behavior. Verified: 7 new retention tests + rewritten record-sync case red on HEAD (deleted:1, stray inserted:1) and green after; the two whole-object IngestStats toEqual assertions unchanged (no new field this release — unreadable_retained counter is 2.17.1).
summary: Ingest retention keyed on the filename stem for every file BEFORE parsing — a narrow, named exception to DD-8 (file-wins): an unreadable or mis-keyed file is not a file and cannot win; parseable correctly-named precedence unchanged; an absent file still deletes its row
